A utility class providing numerous static helpers for string manipulation, numeric parsing/formatting, container streaming, hex/binary conversions, type demangling, and more. It also defines an inner helper class StringStreamWrapper for pooled stringstream usage. Constructors and destructor are declared but behavior is static-only; most functionality does not require instances.

Utility class providing static functions for retrieving current wall-clock and monotonic time at various resolutions and converting between time units. Also formats times into strings. No instances or state; all methods are static. Construction/destruction not applicable.

RAII helper that measures elapsed monotonic time in microseconds for the lifetime of the object and accumulates it into a provided int64_t reference. Construct with a counter reference; upon destruction, adds elapsed microseconds to that counter.

RAII stopwatch capturing start time at construction using monotonic microseconds. Provides query methods for elapsed time in seconds, milliseconds, and microseconds. Does not automatically record on destruction.

Utility to measure durations of successive stages. Call end_stage() to close a stage; the duration is stored in _lastStageUs and can be read via last_us()/last_ms()/last_sec(). Uses monotonic microseconds for timing.
RAII-style wrapper around pthread_mutex_t providing lock/trylock/unlock with thread-annotation macros. Manages pthread_mutex lifecycle.
Mutex subclass initialized with recursive mutex attributes, allowing the same thread to lock multiple times. The static attribute pointer is declared here; definition likely in a source file.
Condition variable combined with an internal mutex. Provides wait (optionally timed), signal, and broadcast operations managing pthread_cond_t lifecycle.
Condition variable with an internal counter to accumulate notifications. signalCounted increments count and signals; waitCounted waits until count > 0 then decrements.
A single mutex with two condition variables to coordinate producers and consumers separately, supporting wait/signal/broadcast for each side.
RAII guard acquiring a ThreadMutex on construction and releasing on destruction. Non-copyable.
Wrapper around pthread_rwlock_t with configurable preference for readers or writers, exposing rdlock/wrlock/try* and unlock. Manages lifecycle.
RAII read lock guard for ReadWriteLock acquiring shared lock on construction and releasing on destruction. Non-copyable.
RAII write lock guard for ReadWriteLock acquiring exclusive lock on construction and releasing on destruction. Non-copyable.
RAII guard for ReadWriteLock that chooses read or write mode at runtime based on a mode character. Unlocks on destruction if a valid mode was used. Non-copyable.
Notification helper using an internal ThreadCond to accumulate and consume notifications with optional exit signaling. EXITED constant is declared but defined elsewhere.
Abstract interface for a termination callback. Implement Run() to execute cleanup logic; lifetime management is external or self-deleting per comments.

Reference-count-like termination coordinator. Threads call inc/dec around work; when count reaches zero, waiters are notified and optional TerminateClosure is run once. EXITED code available; notifyExit is commented out.
Simple ticket spinlock data structure exposing two atomics: users (next ticket) and ticket (current owner). Locking is performed externally (see ScopedTicketSpinLock).
RAII guard implementing a ticket spinlock using TicketSpinLock’s atomics. On construction, acquires a ticket and spins until granted; on destruction, advances the ticket.
Lightweight spinlock built on std::atomic_flag. Busy-waits in lock() until it can acquire; unlock() clears the flag.
RAII guard for SpinLock acquiring on construction and releasing on destruction. Non-copyable.

A small-string-optimized string class in namespace autil. Stores up to BUF_SIZE-1 chars inline in an internal buffer; longer strings allocate dynamically. Provides constructors from C strings, std::string, ranges; assignment, concatenation operator+= (declared here, definition likely in a source file), and standard string-like accessors/iterators. Null-terminates internal storage and exposes c_str(). Memory is freed in destructor; clear() resets to inline buffer. Friend ShortStringTest suggests unit tests. Comparison and stream operators are defined inline in this header. Details like operator+= behavior are not shown here and must be checked in implementation.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate interesting, valid null-terminated C strings (writable) for:
# - StringUtil::toUpperCase/toLowerCase: any null-terminated, including various char ranges
# - ShortString::operator= / assign(const char*): expects a valid null-terminated C string; size becomes strlen(before first NUL)
# Therefore: produce a byte buffer that, when interpreted by the harness as FUZZ_PARAM_STR or FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME contents,
# yields diverse strings without embedded NULs before the terminator (since std::string stops before NUL anyway). We ensure
# a trailing NUL is present in the file/buffer to satisfy in-place mutation requirements when copied and push_back('\0').
# We will generate ASCII plus some extended bytes to exercise case mapping and non-alpha behavior, include digits, symbols,
# mixed case, Unicode UTF-8 sequences (treated as bytes), whitespace varieties, hex-like strings, numbers for strTo* consumers,
# and long/short lengths around ShortString BUF_SIZE=48 threshold.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return rng.choice(seq)

def _make_mixed_case_word(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in base:
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.6:
            out.append(ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)

def _utf8_sequences(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Create some valid UTF-8 sequences (2-4 byte codepoints), but avoid embedding NUL
    res = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        typ = rng.randint(2, 4)
        if typ == 2:
            # 0xC2..0xDF 0x80..0xBF
            first = rng.randint(0xC2, 0xDF)
            cont = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            res += bytes([first, cont])
        elif typ == 3:
            first = rng.randint(0xE0, 0xEF)
            # Basic continuation bytes
            b2 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b3 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            # Tweak overlong/invalid avoided; we keep valid ranges loosely
            res += bytes([first, b2, b3])
        else:
            first = rng.randint(0xF0, 0xF4)
            b2 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b3 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            b4 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
            res += bytes([first, b2, b3, b4])
    return bytes(res)

def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; std::string handles bytes fine
    chars = []
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            chars.append(_rand_choice(rng, list(WHITESPACE)))
        else:
            chars.append(_rand_choice(rng, list(PRINTABLE_ASCII)))
    return ''.join(chars)

def _interesting_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    tokens: List[bytes] = []

    # Simple words to exercise case functions
    words = [
        "hello", "WORLD", "MiXeD", "straße", "mañana", "CAFÉ", "naïve", "ß", "İstanbul",
        "abcXYZ123", "json_key", "PATH/To/File.txt", "param=value", "UPPERlower", "camelCase",
    ]
    for w in words:
        tokens.append(w.encode('utf-8'))

    # Numeric forms for potential number parsing (though not in the stub list, they may be used elsewhere)
    nums = ["0", "-1", "127", "128", "255", "65535", "-32768", "2147483647", "-2147483648",
            "4294967295", "9223372036854775807", "-9223372036854775808", "3.14159", "-0.0", "1e10", "-2.5e-3"]
    tokens.extend(x.encode('ascii') for x in nums)

    # Hex strings
    hexes = ["0x0", "0x1A2b3C", "deadBEEF", "0123456789abcdef", "CAFEBABE", "ffff", "7fFFffFF"]
    tokens.extend(h.encode('ascii') for h in hexes)

    # Boolean-like
    bools = ["true", "false", "TRUE", "False", "yes", "no", "on", "off"]
    tokens.extend(b.encode('ascii') for b in bools)

    # Whitespace variations
    ws = [" ", "\t\t", "\r\n", "\n", "\v\f", "   trim me   "]
    tokens.extend(x.encode('ascii') for x in ws)

    # UTF-8 sequences block
    tokens.append(_utf8_sequences(rng, rng.randint(2, 6)))

    # Random ASCII strings of various lengths; include around ShortString::BUF_SIZE boundary (48)
    lengths = [0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 47, 48, 49, 64, 128, 256]
    for ln in lengths:
        if ln == 0:
            tokens.append(b"")
        else:
            tokens.append(_random_ascii(rng, ln).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))

    # Path-like and key=value like
    for _ in range(5):
        key = _make_mixed_case_word(rng, _random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 8)))
        val = _random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 10))
        tokens.append(f"{key}={val}".encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        parts = [
            _make_mixed_case_word(rng, _random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 6)))
            for __ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))
        ]
        tokens.append(('/'.join(parts)).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # Ensure at least one all-lower and all-upper sequence for clear effects
    tokens.append(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
    tokens.append(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")

    return tokens

def _assemble_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    tokens = _interesting_tokens(rng)

    # Choose a subset and join with newlines to provide multiple inputs in one buffer.
    # Many fuzz harnesses will consume the entire buffer as a single string; even then,
    # upper/lower will operate on the whole content. ShortString assign only uses up to first NUL,
    # so we avoid embedded NULs here and add exactly one final NUL terminator.
    count = rng.randint(1, min(12, len(tokens)))
    chosen = rng.sample(tokens, count)

    # Occasionally create a very long token near limit
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        long_len = rng.randint(512, 1500)
        chosen.append(_random_ascii(rng, long_len).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))

    payload = b"\n".join(chosen)

    # Clamp to limit and ensure it doesn't end with an internal NUL
    payload = payload[: max(0, MAX_TOTAL - 1)]

    # Ensure trailing NUL terminator
    return payload + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _assemble_buffer(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: hex string
# We want to generate interesting but valid inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME usages
# in the provided stubs. The stubs exercise:
#  - StringUtil::hexStrToUint64: expects hex strings, sometimes with 0x/0X, lowercase/uppercase
#  - StringUtil::hexStrToInt64: similar expectations
#  - StringUtil::hexStrToStr: expects valid hex text for decode path, or arbitrary for non-assert path
# Our generator will produce bytes that, when interpreted as a string buffer by the fuzzer infra,
# provide:
#  - Valid hex numbers (lower/upper, with/without 0x)
#  - Edge values (0, 1, max 64-bit, values near 2^63 boundary)
#  - Even-length hex payloads to be valid input to hexStrToStr (round-trip possible)
#  - Some random-length valid hex strings (even and odd lengths) to explore decode failure/success
# The buffer is a single bytes object; the harness can read slices to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

HEX_DIGITS_LOWER = "0123456789abcdef"
HEX_DIGITS_UPPER = "0123456789ABCDEF"


def _rand_hex_digits(rng: random.Random, n: int, upper: bool = False) -> str:
    digits = HEX_DIGITS_UPPER if upper else HEX_DIGITS_LOWER
    return "".join(rng.choice(digits) for _ in range(n))


def _u64_to_hex(v: int, upper: bool = False, prefix: bool = False) -> str:
    h = f"{v:016X}" if upper else f"{v:016x}"
    # Trim leading zeros but leave at least one digit
    h = h.lstrip('0') or '0'
    if prefix:
        h = ("0X" if upper else "0x") + h
    return h


def _edge_hex_samples() -> List[int]:
    return [
        0,
        1,
        0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF,
        0x7FFF, 0x8000, 0xFFFF,
        0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF,
        0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 0x8000000000000000, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF,
    ]


def _make_valid_hex_numbers(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Edge values in different renderings
    for v in _edge_hex_samples():
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=False, prefix=False))
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=True, prefix=False))
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=False, prefix=True))
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=True, prefix=True))
    # Random 64-bit values with variety
    for _ in range(12):
        v = rng.getrandbits(64)
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=False, prefix=rng.choice([True, False])))
        out.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=True, prefix=rng.choice([True, False])))
    # Short forms (1-3 digits) and long forms (up to 16)
    for _ in range(8):
        n = rng.randint(1, 16)
        up = rng.choice([True, False])
        pref = rng.choice([True, False])
        s = _rand_hex_digits(rng, n, up)
        if pref:
            s = ("0X" if up else "0x") + s
        out.append(s)
    return out


def _make_hex_text_for_decode(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Create valid even-length hex strings that represent arbitrary bytes
    # Include empty string case for 0-length data
    out.append("")
    # Single byte, multi-byte sequences
    for length in [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 16, 32, 64, 128]:
        up = rng.choice([True, False])
        out.append(_rand_hex_digits(rng, length, up))
    # Random even lengths up to 256
    for _ in range(8):
        length = rng.randrange(0, 130) * 2  # even
        up = rng.choice([True, False])
        out.append(_rand_hex_digits(rng, length, up))
    # Also include some odd-length valid-hex (should be invalid for decode)
    for _ in range(6):
        length = rng.randrange(1, 65) * 2 + 1  # odd
        up = rng.choice([True, False])
        out.append(_rand_hex_digits(rng, length, up))
    return out


def _with_trailing_junk(rng: random.Random, base_hex: str) -> str:
    # Append a single non-hex character to trigger invalid parse in hexStrTo{U}Int64 else-branch
    junk_choices = ["Z", "G", "_", " ", "+", "-", "x"]
    return base_hex + rng.choice(junk_choices)


def _assemble_buffer(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as newline-separated entries so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can consume chunks or the whole
    # The fuzzer infra typically reads arbitrary slices; providing many lines increases variety
    text = "\n".join(strings)
    # Ensure max size
    b = text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[str] = []

    # Section 1: Valid hex numbers in different formats (to satisfy hexStrToUint64/int64)
    valid_nums = _make_valid_hex_numbers(rng)
    rng.shuffle(valid_nums)
    parts.extend(valid_nums[:24])  # keep size reasonable while preserving variety

    # Section 2: Valid hex strings for decode (even-length, upper/lower)
    hex_for_decode = _make_hex_text_for_decode(rng)
    rng.shuffle(hex_for_decode)
    parts.extend(hex_for_decode[:24])

    # Section 3: Trailing junk variants for the parsing stubs
    for _ in range(10):
        base = _u64_to_hex(rng.getrandbits(32), upper=rng.choice([True, False]), prefix=False)
        parts.append(_with_trailing_junk(rng, base))

    # Section 4: Prefixed forms with and without uppercase
    for _ in range(8):
        v = rng.getrandbits(64)
        parts.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=False, prefix=True))
        parts.append(_u64_to_hex(v, upper=True, prefix=True))

    # Section 5: Corner cases for decode: include whitespace-only line which is not valid hex,
    # and a line with only prefix which is invalid for numeric parse but interesting
    parts.extend([" ", "\t", "0x", "0X"])  # these are valid strings but invalid hex payloads

    # Section 6: A round-trip friendly line: represent some ASCII bytes as hex to drive decode success
    sample_bytes = bytearray(rng.choice([
        b"", b"A", b"hello", b"\x00\x01\xFE\xFF", b"HexDecode", b"0123456789abcdef",
    ]))
    # Convert to hex lower/upper
    if rng.choice([True, False]):
        rt = sample_bytes.hex()
    else:
        rt = sample_bytes.hex().upper()
    parts.append(rt)

    # Shuffle final list to mix patterns
    rng.shuffle(parts)

    return _assemble_buffer(parts)
